paper.title: LSNR: Learned Sparse News Recommendations with Attentive User Modeling
paper.summary: Current learned sparse approaches for recommender systems, such as STAR, represent a user by concatenating their interaction history into a single query string. For news, this creates two bottlenecks: concatenation collapses a user's distinct reading interests into one flat query, and, because news articles are long-form text, concatenating several news articles quickly overruns the context window of the language model used as backbone and forces quality-degrading truncation.   To address both bottlenecks, we introduce learned sparse news recommendations (LSNR). LSNR encodes each article independently and constructs a sparse user vector by combining learned, attention-based weighting of the per-article sparse representations with a dense-projected expansion at the user level. Experiments on the MIND and EBNeRD datasets show that LSNR significantly outperforms STAR, with these gains holding even in short-history settings where truncation is not a factor. Compared to state-of-the-art dense recommenders, LSNR is competitive in standard settings and it outperforms them when the user history is short. An ablation of the user encoder confirms that learned attention-based aggregation outperforms simpler pooling alternatives. Beyond effectiveness, an additional advantage of LSNR is that it serves from an index an order of magnitude smaller than an uncompressed dense baseline.
paper.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 9 tables. Accepted at SIGIR-AP 2026

analysis.problem_statement: Current learned sparse recommender systems fail to effectively model diverse user interests in news recommendation due to the flattening of interaction histories into single query strings and the context window limitations imposed by long-form article text.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Context window limitations and information loss from concatenating long-form text sequences in large language model backbones.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the scalability and representational fidelity issues in news recommendation by decoupling article encoding from user history aggregation. It enables the use of long-form text without truncation by processing articles independently, which is critical for maintaining recommendation quality in data-sparse or short-history scenarios.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Outperformance of STAR and competitive performance against state-of-the-art dense recommenders, particularly in short-history settings.
key_metrics.baseline: STAR (Learned Sparse) and State-of-the-Art Dense Recommenders

technical_breakdown.method: LSNR encodes each news article independently to avoid context overflow, then constructs a sparse user vector by applying learned attention-based weighting to per-article sparse representations and adding a dense-projected expansion at the user level.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Independent article encoder, attention-based user aggregation module, and dense projection layer for user-level expansion.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses attention mechanisms to weight per-article sparse representations, replacing simple concatenation or pooling. Serves from a compressed index significantly smaller than uncompressed dense baselines.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Reduces context length requirements per inference step by processing articles independently, though it requires additional computation for attention-based aggregation and dense projection.
